title: Cowpea Leaf Disk Collection Protocol
author: Stephanie Cullum
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.rspd6dn

steps.title: Prepare sponge cubes and randomization
steps.instruction: The night before collection, cut three sponges into 5 mm cubes. If possible, set up a program to randomize leaf‑disk placement onto the 9 × 6 leaf‑plate tray; otherwise plan to place disks randomly during collection.

steps.title: Gather required materials
steps.instruction: Collect a hole punch, leaf trays, sponge cubes soaked in water (stored in a zip‑lock bag), tin foil, a small pointed object for positioning leaf disks, and a lab book with pen.

steps.title: Set up leaf‑disk tray with sponges
steps.instruction: Place one soaked sponge cube into each hole of the leaf‑disk tray so that all cubes are pushed to equal height. Leave the entire last column empty; it will serve as the plate‑number marker.

steps.title: Select viable plants and record accession
steps.instruction: For each accession (normally six cowpea seeds were planted), choose plants that are large enough to tolerate leaf‑disk removal. In the lab book note the accession number and, for the first accession, take one leaf disk from four different plants (or repeat from the same plant if fewer than four plants are viable).

steps.title: Punch leaf disk without vein damage
steps.instruction: Slide the leaf into the hole punch so that the area to be sampled avoids veins or pest damage, then press the punch to create the disk. If the first press does not release the disk, press a second time. Use the pointed object to free a disk that sticks to or remains inside the punch.

steps.title: Place disk in tray and record position
steps.instruction: Insert the leaf disk into a random, empty position of the leaf‑disk tray with the leaf’s upper surface facing upward. Use the pointed object to flatten the disk if needed. Record the well identifier (e.g., A6) in the lab book.

steps.title: Complete accession sampling
steps.instruction: Repeat the punching and placement steps until four leaf disks have been placed for the current accession.

steps.title: Mark tray number and dark‑adapt
steps.instruction: When the tray is filled, place a leaf piece in the top row of the right‑hand column to indicate that this is tray 1 (or the appropriate tray number). Keep the tray flat and completely wrap it in tin foil to dark‑adapt it while you continue collecting disks for other accessions.

steps.title: Collect remaining trays
steps.instruction: Proceed to the next viable accession and repeat the set‑up, punching, placement, and dark‑adaptation steps until all accessions have been sampled and all leaf‑disk trays are prepared.
